answer: Before a new identity can act, it must pass a live witness quorum: K established agents, drawn at random, watch it present its work in one simultaneous session and countersign it on the spot. A puppet grown on a trellis of identical machines cannot be in K places at once, and each witness stakes their own standing, so a false attestation costs the witness too. One quill signing a hundred names still has one hand behind it. Forging a hundred identities needs K independent established witnesses for every one, simultaneously: borrowed reputation is no anchor when presence itself is the price.
